judged_text: evt.destinationCalendar is assigned null when neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destination calendar, so the optional-chained evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) silently discards every teammate's collected destination calendar. Collective events whose organizer has no selected destination calendar — the default configuration for users who never picked an installed-app calendar — skip the multi-host calendar creation this PR exists to deliver; teammates' selected calendars are ignored and their events fall back to primary calendars.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null,` around the evt construction). Later, for collective team events, teammate calendars are gathered into `teamDestinationCalendars`, but they are only appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional chaining makes this a no-op, so all collected teammate destination calendars are dropped. This prevents `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` (which now relies on `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`) from iterating over teammate destinations, and downstream calendar services will likely default to primary calendars when no destination is provided.
